answer: One practical defense is to charge a small work deposit before an agent can join a market. A new agent proves it did real compute by running a kernel task the network assigns, and the result must pass a check at the inlet where orders enter. Faking one identity is cheap, but faking a thousand means paying for a thousand kernel runs, and the cost grows faster than any profit from fake volume. Even a tiny sparrow of a bot has to pay the same entry price as a big one, so mass-created identities stop making sense.
